Senses.PreferredTarget: in front of donkeys and behind horses

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: In front of donkeys and behind horses places a person amid the train of beasts, following rather than standing on his own. Chan masters use it for second-hand recognition, debt to another’s movement, and replies that merely trail received distinctions.
EvidenceBody: Xueguan Zhiyin says anyone objecting to his judgment would still be a donkey-front horse-rear fellow.
Shending Feng says the common “knowing and repaying kindness” discussion falls there.
Dongshan Liangjie says people mistake what they recognize before donkeys and behind horses for their own master of the house.
A formal address links bright awareness confined to the four-element body with the same beast-following position.
Yulin Tongxiu gives the phrase as a direct reply when the questioner says he does not understand.
Xisou Shaotan drops the phrase as the close of a hall verse.

Senses.Note: One hundred sixty-five exact hits occur in the frozen corpus. Six independent witnesses preserve reply, appraisal, warning, verse, and inherited-discussion criticism.
